title: Informal Economy Database

perception_sources.source: World Economic Forum Executive Opinion Surveys

source_page_claims.count_reconciliation: Count remains unresolved at the observed-series level. The World Bank page lists two output estimates (DGE and MIMIC), four employment indicators, and six perception indicators, which is 12 listed series if DGE and MIMIC are counted separately, versus the page's stated 11 measures. One conceptual output category with two estimators would yield 11 conceptual categories, but the OECD/QoG downstream catalog lists DGE and MIMIC as distinct variables, and a World Bank reproducibility package reports DGE_p and MIMIC_p sheets/variables. The actual official workbook edition and its inventory must be inspected before deciding how the source intends the measure count.

concept_inventory.note: The source page taxonomy supports both a one-concept/two-estimator interpretation and a twelve-series interpretation; downstream catalogs list DGE and MIMIC separately. Do not select an interpretation without inspecting the exact workbook edition.

license_review.general_world_bank_terms_summary: World Bank Data Catalog datasets default to CC BY 4.0 unless specifically labeled otherwise; third-party datasets may have separate restrictions.
license_review.specific_evidence_label: CC BY 4.0 for named informal-economy-database.xlsx row; Custom license in separate package catalog
license_review.interpretation_limit: A specific catalogue row labels the named workbook CC BY 4.0, while another reproduction catalogue labels a workbook source Custom license and links to general terms; a derivative is separately listed CC BY 4.0. The evidence is inconsistent at the catalogue-metadata level. The project gate is not a legal finding that reuse is prohibited; verify the exact current asset and governing terms before project approval.
license_review.required_next_action: Determine whether the actual workbook is governed by the linked World Bank dataset terms or a dataset-specific notice, then record explicit rights evidence for attribution, modification, redistribution, and commercial use before ingestion or publication.

official_asset.label: Informal economy data (Excel)
official_asset.note: The official page links to an Excel download. The bytes have not been retrieved and inspected in this review; do not claim workbook sheet/column inventory or a digest.

reproducibility_package_evidence.interpretation: The package metadata establishes that a 2026 reproduction effort reports the dataset publicly available and included in its package, while applying a Custom license label and linking the World Bank dataset terms. This is availability evidence, not a complete rights analysis. A separate World Bank reproduction package for a different paper describes DGE_p and MIMIC_p sheets in a processed derivative; it is supplementary evidence about downstream variable separation, not proof of the exact current workbook inventory or its license.

cross_catalog_evidence.interpretation_limit: The downstream catalog treats DGE and MIMIC as separately selectable variables. This corroborates distinct series in that catalog; it does not establish the exact sheet/column inventory of the current World Bank Excel workbook.

cross_catalog_evidence.source_context: The package documents a processed derivative of the Informal Economy Database and a distinct additional author-provided file. Its column names and license terms must not be assumed to match the current official Excel workbook.

license_evidence_matrix.access_policy_label: Publicly available and will be included in the package
license_evidence_matrix.caveat: The same catalogue page states in its package-level overview that the RR_WLD_2025_286 ZIP is under temporary embargo and its reproduction data/code are not yet publicly available, while its separate dataset row identifies the original informal-economy-database.xlsx as publicly available and included. Do not fetch or redistribute the embargoed package. Treat this as a scope ambiguity in catalogue metadata; the official page exposes its own direct Excel link, which must be retrieved and verified independently.

rights_adjudication.not_a_legal_finding: The project gate is precautionary and does not assert that the dataset is legally prohibited from reuse.
rights_adjudication.reconciliation_note: One World Bank reproduction catalogue specifically identifies the named Excel workbook and labels it CC BY 4.0, while the overview on that same catalogue page marks its parent reproduction ZIP as temporarily embargoed and says its reproduction data/code are not yet publicly available; a separate row on that page says the original dataset is public and included. A second catalogue lists DGE_Raw.xlsx under Custom license, and a third labels a processed derivative CC BY 4.0. These statements have different scopes and cannot be reconciled solely from labels. Verify the original official Excel asset directly and its current terms before project approval.
